chunks.content: # Designer’s CLO Journey: Dopamine Style Top Revision (Gathering Section) This document provides a detailed walkthrough of modifying two distinct tops in CLO 3D: a smocker top and a draw-structured pink top. It covers garment modeling, editing patterns and lines, applying elasticity and seam allowances, fabric adjustments, and simulation optimization techniques for realistic folds and fit. --- ## Smocker Top Modification Workflow This section details the step-by-step process of modifying a basic long-sleeve t-shirt into a smocker top using CLO 3D tools such as edit shape line, edit sheet, and inner multi-sided line. It includes pattern adjustments, seam allowance setup, elasticity application based on model body data, and simulation tips for realistic fabric behavior. ### Initial Model Setup and Basic Adjustments - Insert the 3D model and a basic long-sleeve knit t-shirt pattern. - Observe the shoulder line, which is initially too long; roughly mark the desired new position. - Use the **Edit Shape Line** tool from the 3D toolbar to adjust the shoulder line. - Switch to the **Edit Sheet** tool to modify the length of the shirt by selecting and pulling the bottom line. - Input precise values in the moving distance spring that appears to control adjustments. - Run simulation frequently to observe changes. ### Front Chest Division and Inner Line Creation - To create a front chest division, use the **Inner Multi-sided Line** tool in the 2D window to draw a line inside the pattern. - Switch to **Edit Sheet** tool and align the inner line to the outside edge of the panel. - Toggle the 3D window to opaque mode for precise placement of the inner line relative to the model. - Repeat the inner line drawing on the back piece to maintain alignment between front and back. - Select both inner lines (front and back) and apply an inner line border of 40 mm, adjustable depending on style and body length. ### Cutting, Enlarging, and Adjusting Pieces - Select the two inner lines at the top and bottom and perform a **Cut and Sew** operation. - Enlarge the middle panel by activating its center point (double-click) and inputting a value of 120 to scale both front and back pieces. - Shrink the middle panel based on model body data obtained from the **Virtual Model Editor**, considering chest and waist measurements. - Use elasticity ratios to control fabric stretch along inner lines, setting proportions typically around 50–65%, but adjustable based on fabric properties and desired effect. ### Applying Elasticity and Simulation Observations - Apply elasticity to inner lines and bottom edges using model body data as references. - For example, elasticity values near the bottom of the chest are smaller than those at the waist. - Use simulation to observe fit; chest area remains tight while the waist is relaxed. - Adjust posture to stoop mode to better observe the garment’s middle section and waist tightness.

Perform shoulder splits by lengthening straight edges and adjusting waist position. - Change inner line lengths (e.g., from 10 or 15 mm to 15 mm). - Create two inner lines, cut and sew them, then merge lines using the edit tool. - Convert points to free curve points and adjust curves for smoothness, deleting unnecessary curve points. - Expand front piece by activating its center point and scaling by 125%. ### Seam Allowance and Fold Creation on Sleeves - Add seam allowance to shoulder and sleeve panels. - Mark division points on shoulders to create fold effects at sleeve tops. - Cut sewing lines into sections corresponding to marked divisions using the **Free Sewing Tool**. - Extend board lines by set distances (e.g., +120 mm, +80 mm) and adjust curves for natural shapes. - Create a 20 mm inner line on sleeves to facilitate back sleeve fold. - Fold lines should be at 0 degrees with dimensions approximately 170 mm wide and 20 mm high. - Seam allowance on these fold lines should be verified as folded, not pinned or left loose. ### Elastic Band Application on Small Panels - Apply new fabric with elastic band properties (feature introduced in CLO 7.2) to small gold panels. - Select elastic band presets: real elastic or shrunken elastic. - Adjust elastic band diameter and gap thickness (set to 1 mm) before simulation. - Extend lower panels by selecting lines, moving them outward by 100 mm or more to create flare or lift at the hem. ### Fabric Adjustments and Final Simulation - Hide the model temporarily to observe fabric behavior without obstruction. - Apply softer or translucent fabrics to specific pieces, visible in high-quality mode. - Improve clothing quality by gradually reducing particle diameters in simulated panels to enhance fold realism. - Keep particle diameter reductions moderate (e.g., step down to 8 before 5) to balance simulation speed and detail. - Add seam allowance and intensity settings to maintain shape and fold effects. --- ## Draw Structure Pink Top Modification Workflow This section covers modifying a shoulder strap top downloaded from the Kinect website. It includes pattern adjustment, line editing, elasticity application, layering, and adding detailed features such as buttons and butterfly knots.

It includes pattern adjustment, line editing, elasticity application, layering, and adding detailed features such as buttons and butterfly knots. ### Pattern Insertion and Basic Line Editing - Insert the model and import the basic shoulder strap pattern. - Lock the outer lines and convert all internal lines to basic lines using the **Edit Pattern** tool. - Unlock the basic line and convert extra points to free line points for easier editing. - Measure shoulder strap length (e.g., 184.6 cm) and modify by deleting curve points, straightening lines, and increasing length by approximately 40 mm (total ~224 mm). - Ensure front and back shoulder straps and side bones have equal lengths. ### Sleeve and Side Bone Adjustments - Adjust breastbone shape and side bone length using the edit tool. - Modify sleeve shape by deleting excess curve points and adjusting curves. - Reduce sleeve height by the same amount shoulder straps were lengthened (e.g., 40 mm), marking reference points for alignment. - Extend sleeve width slightly and preview changes in the 3D window. ### Side Gap and Bottom Shape Adjustments - Rotate side angles by 5 degrees to align front and back pieces. - Move rotation center points appropriately to maintain symmetry. - Adjust the back piece bottom shape by lowering center points and smoothing curves. - Check the connection of side bones to ensure clean corners. ### 3D Pen Tool for Line Drawing and Elasticity Setup - Use the 3D pen tool in the 3D window to draw new lines and adjust their positions. - Add curve points with Ctrl key to refine lines. - Display internal lines to verify placement. - Set elasticity ratios for new lines (e.g., 60%, adjusting as needed). - Fill missing seam lines caused by stretching with appropriate sewing. ### Sleeve Volume and Positioning - Use external expansion or shrink tools to modify sleeve volume, setting diameter and height (e.g., 50 mm). - Align sleeve cuff opening behind the model’s hand for natural fit. - Adjust X-axis components: width 20 mm, height 130 mm. - Use edit board tool to divide and delete unnecessary lines; add points to outer lines. - Create cross-sectional lines and sew components with free sewing tools. - Set folds with 5 mm allowance and switch to fold mode. ### Sleeve Sewing, Button Placement, and Symmetry - Reduce board width to increase width elsewhere as needed. - Flip boards to ensure middle parts face outward. - Sew sleeves separately, then sew all parts together using Shift key.

chunks.content: - Use edit board tool to divide and delete unnecessary lines; add points to outer lines. - Create cross-sectional lines and sew components with free sewing tools. - Set folds with 5 mm allowance and switch to fold mode. ### Sleeve Sewing, Button Placement, and Symmetry - Reduce board width to increase width elsewhere as needed. - Flip boards to ensure middle parts face outward. - Sew sleeves separately, then sew all parts together using Shift key. - Add buttons by right-clicking on board edges, setting equal distances (e.g., 25 mm vertically, 10 mm horizontally). - Adjust button size and orientation; ensure button and buttonhole do not flip incorrectly. - Copy and paste buttons symmetrically on the opposite side. - Set sewing layers for buttons and seam allowances. - Simulate and adjust to ensure proper fit and appearance. ### Front Structure and Drawstring Positioning - Use edit panel tool to cut seam allowances and create 10 mm internal lines around drawstring positions. - Add elasticity (e.g., 50%) to these internal lines. - Combine small panels into a joint by merging outer edges. - Avoid merging too early to preserve symmetry during detail adjustments. ### Fabric and Fold Quality Adjustments - Change fabric to cotton or a foldable type. - Reduce particle diameter gradually to improve fold detail without significant slowdowns. - Adjust fold textures and simulate repeatedly to refine appearance. - Use fixing pins for stable simulation, removing them (Ctrl+D) when no longer needed. - Observe details, especially at fold points and seams, enhancing realism. ### Butterfly Knot Creation and Positioning - Locate nodes for butterfly knot attachment; import clothing files as needed. - Draw and adjust inner lines for sewing butterfly knots onto the garment. - Use the panel and 3D window to align seams and ensure matching seam allowances. - Butterfly knots require smaller particle diameters, increasing simulation time. - Apply shrinkage effects to knots for realistic tension. - Freeze unrelated parts during simulation to reduce computational load. - Copy and mirror butterfly knots to maintain symmetry. - Adjust knot tail lengths by unlinking symmetrical sides and modifying individually. ### Final Touches: Neckline, Stickers, and Color - Select neckline center and apply 100% elasticity. - Add stickers around neckline and sides for detailing. - Adjust sticker widths and conflict thickness for correct layering. - Apply consistent coloring to buttons, stickers, and bright lines for cohesive appearance. - Adjust bright lines to be more prominent by applying brighter colors. - Save the final file after confirming all adjustments. --- ##
